supplements.exploratory: Read through the whole source before selecting material; the opening event can supply context while later passages carry the article's distinctive focus. Give sentence space to distinct central developments or perspectives, rather than repeated setup, vivid scene-setting, or several details about the same event. A prominent response or conclusion can be central even when it contains no numerical result. For strict extraction, consider candidate sentence combinations as a whole: prefer those that jointly retain the main event and another central aspect with clear referents and intact attribution. Do not automatically copy an opening sentence merely to introduce a name. Keep context necessary to understand selected sentences; when that context would consume the available budget, choose a clearer combination. When rewriting is permitted, combine compatible source clauses only when their subjects, status, and attribution remain clear. Use additional permitted space to preserve substantive distinctions, not repetition. Apply all base constraints throughout; do not lengthen a short extractive summary or alter copied sentences to force in every point.

not_adoption: Selected here for evaluation only; no automatic product replacement.
